Regulation: B.C. Reg. 106/2026
Made under: Correction Act
Published in: No. 12 – B.C. Regs. 99 to 109, June 30, 2026
Deposit date: June 26, 2026

B.C. Reg. 106/2026, deposited June 26, 2026, under theCORRECTION ACT[section 33] andMISCELLANEOUS STATUTES AMENDMENT ACT, 2026[section 33]. Order in Council 266/2026, approved and ordered June 26, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that (a)	sections 28 to 32 of theMiscellaneous Statutes Amendment Act, 2026, S.B.C. 2026, c. 15, are brought into force, and (b)	section 9 (1) of the Correction Act Regulation, B.C. Reg. 58/2005, is amended by striking out "or" at the end of paragraph (c), by adding ", or" at the end of paragraph (d) and by adding the following paragraph: (e)	assist a treatment provider to give treatment to an inmate, as described in section 12 of the Act. — N. KRIEGER,Minister of Public Safety and Solicitor General; J. OSBORNE,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. minutes_briefs.title: BC correctional regulation updated to let inmates assist treatment providers
minutes_briefs.summary: British Columbia has updated its Correction Act Regulation to allow inmates to help treatment providers give treatment to other inmates, as described in section 12 of the Act. This change was made official on June 26, 2026, and is now in force. It affects how treatment is delivered inside provincial correctional facilities.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you operate a business providing treatment services inside BC correctional facilities, review your staffing and supervision practices to account for inmate assistants.
